newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end up on better earnings prospects.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end up on better earnings prospects.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher in active trading on Wednesday as investors built up holdings ahead of quarterly results due to be released shortly, brokers said.
"The market, which has been searching for direction for so long, is rising in anticipation of good corporate results for the quarter to September 30," said a trader at brokerage John Keells.
The all share index closed 4.15 points higher at 599.67. Gainers led decliners by 37 to four. Central Finance rose 2.50 rupees to 245 and National Development Bank three to 195.
While retail investors were in the driving seat, local and foreign institutions were also picking selected stocks, brokers said.
"With every point the index gains it becomes easier to find sellers in bulk," Dimantha Kohombanwickramage of NDBS Stock Brokers said, adding this would increase trade volume.

Turnover was 65.62 million rupees, backed by foreign buying of 580,000 Sampath Bank, which rose 50 cents to 46.50 rupes, and local institutional buying of 202,000 Seylan Bank, which gained one rupee to 26 rupees.
